turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Um, I came in because... well, I drive a cab, and even when I know for a fact I did my safety check on the car, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something. 

I keep thinking that because I messed up, somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna say I lied about doing the check in the first place. It's just... I can't make the thought shut up. It's in my head the whole time I'm driving, or even when I'm just trying to sit down and study. It's really getting to be too much.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports recurrent, intrusive, and uncontrollable thoughts of having missed safety checks and causing harm, fitting the criteria for obsessions.

turns.doctor_question: When you get these thoughts about missing the safety check, do you find yourself going back to double-check the car, or doing anything else repeatedly to try to make the thought go away?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Um, before I can even take a ride, I just... I keep going around the car. I check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, all my paperwork. And I do it over and over. 

Sometimes I even take pictures of everything on my phone, and if something just doesn't feel right, I have to restart the whole check from the very beginning. I end up doing this even when I have passengers standing there waiting for me and I'm already late. I just have to do it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes engaging in repetitive checking rituals (inspecting the car, tires, lights, doors, taking pictures, and restarting from the beginning if it doesn't feel right) repeatedly even when late, confirming compulsions.
